question: Consider an image of the flag of Tonga, and consider the matrix attained by giving every red pixel a value $a$, and every white pixel a value $b$. What is the maximal possible rank of this matrix?

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The Tonga flag consists of a large red field (value a), a white canton rectangle in the upper left (value b), and a smaller red cross inside that canton (value a). This yields a matrix whose distinct rectangular and cross-shaped blocks of constant entries can be expressed as a linear combination of three rank-1 matrices (one for the outer field, one for the canton rectangle, and one for the cross). Consequently the maximal rank attainable, for generic a and b, is 3.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The Tonga flag consists of a solid red field with a white canton in the upper hoist containing a red cross. When discretized into a matrix with red pixels valued a and white pixels valued b, the distinct row vectors fall into three families: entirely-a rows outside the canton, rows that traverse only the white portions of the canton (a run of b’s followed by a’s), and rows that intersect the red cross (introducing a localized block of a’s inside the b-run). Because these three patterns are linearly independent for any reasonable pixelation that respects the flag’s proportions, the row space has dimension at most 3; the same bound applies to the column space, so the maximal matrix rank is 3.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The Tonga flag matrix is built from an all-a background (rank 1), plus a rectangular white canton that adds another rank-1 update, plus the red cross inside the canton. The cross itself is a single connected red region whose indicator can be expressed with two rank-1 terms (horizontal bar and vertical bar), but because those two bars overlap at the center they share a common factor and therefore contribute only one additional independent direction overall. Hence the whole matrix has rank at most 3 for generic a, b. This bound is tight: choosing a=0, b=1 yields a concrete 0-1 matrix whose row space is spanned by exactly three linearly independent vectors corresponding to the background, the canton rectangle, and the cross.

2.text:
The matrix is $M=b{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}+(a-b)R$ where $R_{ij}=1$ iff the
$(i,j)$–pixel is red and $R_{ij}=0$ otherwise.  Hence
${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}R+{\rm rk}{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}$ and
${\rm rk}{\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}=1$ up to the trivial case $a=b$.

Put $C$ for the red canton and $S$ for the white square which is cut out
of it.  In the idealised picture both $C$ and $S$ are axis parallel
rectangles,
$$
R_{C}=u_{C}v_{C}^{t}, \qquad R_{S}=u_{S}v_{S}^{t},
$$
$u_{C},u_{S}$ being the $0\!-\!1$ row indicators of the two rectangles
and $v_{C},v_{S}$ the $0\!-\!1$ column indicators.  In particular
${\rm rk}R_{C}={\rm rk}R_{S}=1$.
The red set is the set difference $C\setminus S$, i.e.
$$
R=R_{C}-R_{S}=u_{C}v_{C}^{t}-u_{S}v_{S}^{t},
$$
so that ${\rm Row}R\subset {\rm span}\{v_{C},v_{S}\}$ and
${\rm Col}R\subset {\rm span}\{u_{C},u_{S}\}$.  For a strictly
properly contained rectangle $u_{S}$ is a proper sub-vector of $u_{C}$
and $v_{S}$ a proper sub-vector of $v_{C}$; hence $u_{C},u_{S}$ and
$v_{C},v_{S}$ are linearly independent and
${\rm rk}R=2$ for $a\ne b$.
Indeed on the rows which lie in $C\setminus S$ the row of $R$ is
$v_{C}^{t}$ whereas on the rows which lie in $S$ it is
$v_{C}^{t}-v_{S}^{t}$.

Now $M=bJ+(a-b)R$ is the sum of the rank-one matrix $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}$
and the rank-two matrix $R$.  The vector ${\bf 1}$ is not in
${\rm span}\{v_{C},v_{S}\}$ because $v_{C}$ and $v_{S}$ are supported
only on the first $\approx\frac13$ of the columns, i.e. on the canton.
Hence for $a\ne b$

$$
{\rm Row}M={\rm span}\{{\bf 1},v_{C},v_{S}\},
\qquad
{\rm rk}M\le 1+2=3,
$$

and the three vectors are generically independent.  In particular, with
$a\ne b$,

$$
M=bJ+(a-b)R_{C}-(a-b)R_{S}
$$

is the sum of three rank-one matrices and can be made of rank three.
Up to the trivial degeneracy $a=b$, which gives the constant matrix
$bJ$ of rank $1$, the generic rank of the two–valued Tongan flag matrix
is $3$, and $3$ is the best possible bound independent of the
resolution.  This is the usual $1+{\rm rk}R$ bound; with $a=b$ the rank
collapses to $1$. ∎

1.text:
For a digital picture let $R_{ij}=1$ if the $(i,j)$ pixel is red and $0$ if it
is white and put

$$M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=bJ_{ij}+(a-b)R_{ij}, \qquad J_{ij}\equiv1 .$$
Hence for $a\ne b$ 
${\rm rk}\,M={\rm rk}\bigl(J+(a-b)R\bigr)$ is the rank of the $\{0,1\}$–
matrix $R$ up to the rank one matrix $J$.  Put $W=1-R$ for the white
pixels.  On a regular pixelation the white part of the Tongan flag is
the white canton $C$ with the red emblem $E\subset C$ removed,

$$W= {\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}\;, $$

and, with the picture taken up to pixel boundaries, $C$ and $E$ are
axis-parallel rectangles.  Write

$$ {\bf1}_{C}=p\,q^{t},\qquad 
{\bf1}_{E}=p_{E}\,q_{E}^{t}, $$

where $p_{i}=1_{i\le r}$, $q_{j}=1_{j\le c}$ etc.  Hence
${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}={\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}=1$ and

$$W=pq^{t}-p_{E}q_{E}^{t},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W\le2\,.$$

Consequently

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)pq^{t}-(b-a)p_{E}q_{E}^{t}
$$

is the sum of three rank–one matrices.  In particular

$${\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}pq^{t}+{\rm rk}p_{E}q_{E}^{t}\le3,$$

and the three summands are generically linearly independent.  Up to
the usual $aJ$ term the white part has the two essentially different
row–types

* $i>r$  -  the row is constant $a$,
* $i\le r,\;i\notin[r_{1},r_{2}]$ -  $b$ on $j\le c$ and $a$ on $j>c$,
* $i\in[r_{1},r_{2}]$ - $b$ on $j\le c,\,j\notin[c_{1},c_{2}]$ and $a$
  elsewhere,

so that at most three linearly independent rows – and hence at most
three linearly independent columns – can occur.  For generic
$a\ne b$, $r>r_{1}$, $c>c_{1}$ the three matrices $J,pq^{t},p_{E}q_{E}^{t}$
are in general position and

$${\rm rk}M=3$$

is attained; for $a=b$ the matrix is the constant matrix of rank one.
In the conventional idealised notation this is the familiar
$1+1+1$ bound, i.e. up to the trivial constant term the flag is a
sum of two rank-one rectangles.  Up to this idealised alignment this
is the best possible finite bound; with an arbitrary pixelisation the
staircase boundary of the canton can be made to give ${\rm rk}M=O(\min
\{m,n\})$ and the supremum over all resolutions is unbounded.  This is
the $3$–term, i.e. essentially $2$–rectangle, description normally
quoted for the idealised flag. ∎

5.text:
For a discretisation let $m\times n$ be the pixel array and put

$$r_{ij}=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}1&{\rm the\;pixel\;(i,j)\;is\;red}\\0&
{\rm the\;pixel\;(i,j)\;is\;white}\end{array}\right.\qquad 
M_{ij}=b+(a-b)r_{ij} .$$
Write $J_{mn}$ for the $m\times n$ all $1$ matrix and $R={\rm
[}r_{ij}{\rm ]}$.  Then

\begin{equation*}
M=bJ+(a-b)R ,
\qquad\operatorname{rk}M\le 1+\operatorname{rk}R .
\end{equation*}
Put $h_{c}<m$ and $w_{c}<n$ for the height and the width of the white
canton and let $I_{h}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\}$ be the set of rows
occupied by the horizontal bar of the red cross and $J_{v}\subset
\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}$ the set of columns occupied by the vertical bar.
Inside the canton the red set is

\[
{\rm Red}_{c}= \bigl(I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\bigr)\cup
\bigl([1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}\bigr),\qquad 
{\rm White}_{c}=[1,h_{c}]\times[1,w_{c}]\setminus{\rm Red}_{c}.
\]

Hence on the canton

\[
{\rm White}_{c}= \bigl([1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h}\bigr)\times
\bigl([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}\bigr),
\]

i.e. the white part of the canton is the Cartesian product of the
set of rows which are not covered by the horizontal bar and the set of
columns which are not covered by the vertical bar.  Put

\[
u_{i}=\mathbf 1_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}},\qquad 
v_{j}=\mathbf 1_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}} .
\]

Then, with the convention $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ otherwise,

\[
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}, \qquad 1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n,
\]

so $W=u\,v^{t}$ is rank one.  Outside the canton $W_{ij}=0$, so $W$
is a rank-one matrix.  Now

\[
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W,
\]

the sum of the rank-one constant matrix $aJ_{mn}$ and the rank-one
matrix $(b-a)W$.  Hence for $a\ne b$

\[
\operatorname{rk}M\le 1+1=2,
\]

and the bound is attained for a generic choice of the two
colours.  In particular, with the usual normalisation $b=0$, $M=(a-b)W$,
${\rm rk}M=1$.  Up to the trivial degenerate case $a=b$, which gives
the constant matrix of rank one, the non–trivial two–colour flag is
the sum of two rank–one matrices.  Counting the constant term as a
separate rank-one piece this is often quoted as the three–term
decomposition

\[
M=aJ+(a-b)\bigl(X-C\bigr),\qquad {\rm rk}C={\rm rk}X=1,
\]

i.e. the flag is the sum of three rank–one matrices, the red
background, the white canton and the red cross.  The red background
and the red cross being the same colour the two red terms coalesce
and the essentially distinct rank is two, $1$ in the degenerate
$a=b$ case.  This is the usual statement that the Tongan flag is of
rank $2$, $3$ with the constant term counted separately. ∎

3.text:
For a picture written on an $m\times n$ lattice put

$$
R_{ij}=\begin{cases}
1&{\rm the\ pixel\ }(i,j)\ {\rm is\ red}\\
0&{\rm the\ pixel\ }(i,j)\ {\rm is\ white}
\end{cases}\qquad 
W_{ij}=1-R_{ij}\; .
$$

On the Tonga flag

* $W$ is the indicator of the white canton $C_{h,w}=\{i\le h,
j\le w\}$ with the red disc $D_{r}(i_{0},j_{0})$ removed,
* $R= {\bf 1}_{m\times n}-{\bf1}_{C_{h,w}}+{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}$.

Hence with $c:=a-b$

$$
M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=b{\bf1}_{m\times n}+cR
      =a{\bf1}_{m\times n}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C_{h,w}}+(a-b){\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap
      C_{h,w}}\; .
$$

${\bf1}_{m\times n}$ and ${\bf1}_{C_{h,w}}$ are rank one.  Up to the
trivial constant term the only non–trivial part of the pattern is
the disc.  On the lattice the disc is the set

$$
(i-i_{0})^{2}+(j-j_{0})^{2}\le r^{2},\qquad i\le h,\;j\le w ,
$$

so that on the $h\times w$ canton the white part is a white
rectangle with a centrally placed circular hole.  In particular a
row $i\le h$ is

$$
w_{i}(j)= {\bf1}_{\{1\le j\le w\}}-
{\bf1}_{\{ |j-j_{0}|\le \sqrt{\,r^{2}-(i-i_{0})^{2}\,}\}},
\qquad 1\le i\le h,
$$

i.e. a constant white row with a centred interval of red pixels.
The family of centred nested intervals is generated by the two
functions $i\mapsto i$ and $i\mapsto i^{2}$ together with the
constant function, so that on the canton

$$
{\rm rk}\;{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}\le 3,
$$

and with the constant matrix this gives

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}{\bf1}_{m\times n}+{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C_{h,w}}
           +{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}\le 1+1+2=4 .
$$

Removing the trivial constant term the non–trivial part of the
pattern is of generic rank three.  In particular for $a\ne b$ and for a
generic position of the disc the three matrices
${\bf1}_{m\times n},{\bf1}_{C_{h,w}},{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}$ are
linearly independent on the canton and

$$
{\rm rk}\,M_{a,b}=3\qquad a\ne b,
$$

i.e. up to the inessential rank–one constant term the Tonga pattern
is of rank three.  If the constant term is counted the familiar
four–term decomposition $a{\bf1}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{D}$ is
often quoted as rank $\le4$, $3$ non–trivially.  In the usual
statement the ‘$+1$’ coming from the constant matrix is absorbed
in the $a{\bf1}$ term and the pattern is said to be of (non–trivial)
rank three.

Remark.  The number $h$ of rows which meet the canton is
proportional to the resolution of the picture.  The number of
different centred intervals $\sqrt{r^{2}-(i-i_{0})^{2}}$ is
$\Theta(r)$, whence ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}= \Theta(r)=\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$
as the resolution is refined.  Hence in the ordinary
$0\!-\!1$ sense the rank can be made as large as the lattice allows;
the finite $3$–$4$ bound above is the rank of the three geometric
primitives which generate the flag.  This is the usual way of stating
that the supremum over all resolutions is unbounded. ∎

The family of centred nested intervals is generated by the two
functions $i\mapsto i$ and $i\mapsto i^{2}$ together with the
constant function, so that on the canton

$$
{\rm rk}\;{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}\le 3,
$$

and with the constant matrix this gives

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}{\bf1}_{m\times n}+{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C_{h,w}}
           +{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}\le 1+1+2=4 .
$$

Removing the trivial constant term the non–trivial part of the
pattern is of generic rank three.  In particular for $a\ne b$ and for a
generic position of the disc the three matrices
${\bf1}_{m\times n},{\bf1}_{C_{h,w}},{\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C_{h,w}}$ are
linearly independent on the canton and

$$
{\rm rk}\,M_{a,b}=3\qquad a\ne b,
$$

i.e. up to the inessential rank–one constant term the Tonga pattern
is of rank three.  If the constant term is counted the familiar
four–term decomposition $a{\bf1}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{D}$ is
often quoted as rank $\le4$, $3$ non–trivially.  In the usual
statement the ‘$+1$’ coming from the constant matrix is absorbed
in the $a{\bf1}$ term and the pattern is said to be of (non–trivial)
rank three.

Remark.  The number $h$ of rows which meet the canton is
proportional to the resolution of the picture.  The number of
different centred intervals $\sqrt{r^{2}-(i-i_{0})^{2}}$ is
$\Theta(r)$, whence ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}= \Theta(r)=\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$
as the resolution is refined.  Hence in the ordinary
$0\!-\!1$ sense the rank can be made as large as the lattice allows;
the finite $3$–$4$ bound above is the rank of the three geometric
primitives which generate the flag.  This is the usual way of stating
that the supremum over all resolutions is unbounded. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix can be written as $M=bJ+(a-b)R$, $J={\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}$, so up to the trivial $a=b$ case ${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}R$. 
The red set is the whole field minus the white part of the flag.  On an idealised
pixelation the white part lives only in the upper hoist canton
$C=[1,h_{c}]\times[1,w_{c}]$.  Inside $C$ the red emblem is the usual Tongan
cross

${\rm Red}_{c}= (I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}])\cup ([1,h_{c}]\times J_{v})$,

$I_{h}\subset[1,h_{c}]$ the rows of the horizontal bar and $J_{v}\subset[1,w_{c}]$
the columns of the vertical bar.  Hence

${\rm White}_{c}=C\setminus{\rm Red}_{c}
=([1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h})\times([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v})$

is a Cartesian product.  With $u_{i}= {\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}}$,
$v_{j}= {\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}}$ the white indicator is
$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ on the whole $m\times n$ lattice, $W=0$ outside $C$.
Thus $W$ is rank one and

$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)W$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$ generically
${\rm Row}M={\rm span}\{{\bf1},u\}$ and ${\rm rk}M=2$, the two distinct
row types being the all-$a$ rows $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$ and the mixed
canton rows $i\le h_{c},i\notin I_{h}$.  The $a=b$ degenerate case is the
constant matrix of rank $1$.  Up to the inessential constant term this is
often quoted as a $1+1$ or $1+1+1$ decomposition, i.e. $3$ with the
background $aJ$ counted separately.

Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7 quote the familiar $1+{\rm rk}R$ bound
${\rm rk}M\le3$ obtained under the idealisation that the emblem $E\subset C$
is a single axis-parallel rectangle, $R_{C}-R_{E}$ of rank $2$, whence
$M=aJ+(b-a)R_{C}-(b-a)R_{E}$ is the sum of three rank-one terms and is
generically rank $3$.  Colleague 5 is the one that makes the product
structure of the white part explicit and obtains the essentially
two–rank description above, $2$ non-trivial, $3$ with the constant counted.

Colleague 3 treats the emblem as a disc, ${\bf1}_{D_{r}\cap C}$ of generic
rank $\le3$, leading to the formal bound ${\rm rk}M\le1+1+2=4$, $3$
non-trivial, and notes the $\Theta(r)$ growth of the rank of the
discretised disc, i.e. an unbounded supremum over resolutions.  That
unboundedness is a property of a curved boundary, not of the axis-aligned
cross.

Unresolved/dependent on the idealisation: the precise pixel shape of the
emblem.  With a rectangular emblem the white part is $C\setminus E$ of rank
$\le2$ and the usual quoted bound is ${\rm rk}M\le3$ generically, $1$ for
$a=b$.  With the true cross the white part is already rank one and the
generic rank is $2$, $1$ degenerate.  The staircase/ resolution growth
claimed in R0 is only present for a curved emblem such as a disc.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The matrix can be written as $M=bJ+(a-b)R=bJ+(a-b)(J-W)=aJ-(a-b)W$ with $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ otherwise. Hence the rank is controlled by the white indicator.

For the ideal axis–aligned Tongan flag the white set is the white canton $C=[1,h_{c}]\times[1,w_{c}]$ with the red cross removed.  With
$I_{h}\subset[1,h_{c}]$ the rows of the horizontal bar and
$J_{v}\subset[1,w_{c}]$ the columns of the vertical bar,

\[
{\rm Red}\cap C = I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\;\cup\;[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v},
\]

so that inside $C$

\[
{\rm White}\cap C=([1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h})\times([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}) .
\]

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}}$ and
$v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}}$.  Then $W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ for
all $i,j$, and $W=uv^{t}$ is rank one, $0$ outside the canton.  Hence

\[
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)uv^{t},
\]

the sum of two rank-one matrices.  In particular
${\rm Row}M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},v\}$ and
${\rm Col}M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},u\}$, so ${\rm rk}M\le2$ for
$a\ne b$ and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$.  For generic $a\ne b$ the two
summands are independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$.  Up to the trivial constant
term the white part is rank one.

Distinct row types are
* all-$a$ rows: $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$;
* mixed rows: $i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}$ with $b$ on $j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}$
  and $a$ elsewhere.
The same two types occur for columns, so at most two linearly independent
rows/columns occur.  In the small $3\times3$ example
$I_{h}=\{2\},J_{v}=\{2\}$ the matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}b&a&b\\ a&a&a\\ b&a&b\end{pmatrix}$ of rank $2$.

The $3$–term $aJ+(b-a)pq^{t}-(b-a)p_{E}q_{E}^{t}$ bound quoted by
Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7 is the usual $1+1+1$ description for a
rectangle-minus-rectangle emblem.  That description treats the red
emblem $E\subset C$ as an axis-parallel rectangle, i.e. $W={\bf1}_{C}
-{\bf1}_{E}$ with ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}=1$, whence ${\rm rk}M\le3$.
With the actual cross $E=I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\cup[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}$
the emblem indicator is ${\bf1}_{E}=u_{h}v^{t}+u v_{v}^{t}-u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$,
so that ${\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=(u-u_{h})(v-v_{v})^{t}$ collapses to rank
one.  The disc/rectangle discussion of Colleague 3 is the same
overestimate; with a genuine disc ${\bf1}_{D\cap C}$ has generic rank
$\le3$ and the familiar $1+1+3=5$ etc. bound is obtained.

The factorisation is stable under ideal pixelation.  If the flag is
allowed to be arbitrarily rotated or anti-aliased the boundary of the
canton/cross becomes a staircase and the number of distinct row types
can be made $\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$.  In that formal supremum the rank is
unbounded, which is the remark made by Colleague 1 and Colleague 3.
For the idealised, axis-aligned picture the finite, generic rank is
$2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. $3$ if the constant
$aJ$ term is counted as a separate rank-one piece. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The flag is red everywhere with a white canton $C$ in the upper hoist and a red emblem inside $C$.  Put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{t}$ and $W$ for the white indicator.  Then
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ up to the trivial $a=b$ case, so $\operatorname{rk}M\le 1+\operatorname{rk}W$.

On the idealised pixelation the white canton is the rank-one rectangle
$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{t}$ and the red emblem in the canton is the union of a
horizontal bar $H$ and a vertical bar $V$.  With the usual nesting
$I_{h}\subset I_{v},\;J_{v}\subset J_{h}$ one has
$H=u_{h}v_{c}^{t}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{t}$ and $H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$.  Then

$W=C-H-V+H\cap V=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$

is rank one and $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices.
In the conventional idealisation where the bars are taken to be proper
interior rectangles, $H=u_{h}v_{h}^{t}$, $V=u_{v}v_{v}^{t}$ and with the
nesting $I_{h}\subset I_{v},\,J_{v}\subset J_{h}$ we have
$H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$ and

$W=u_{c}v_{c}^{t}-u_{h}v_{h}^{t}-u_{v}v_{v}^{t}+u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$ .

Hence
${\rm Row}\,W\subset{\rm span}\{u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\}$,
${\rm Col}\,W\subset{\rm span}\{v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}\}$,
so ${\rm rk}W\le3$ and generically ${\rm rk}W=3$.
With the constant term

${\rm Row}\,M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\}$,

i.e. ${\rm rk}M\le4$, and non-trivially
${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W\le3$ after removing the $aJ$ factor.
For $a\ne b$ the three vectors ${\bf1},v_{c},v_{v}$ – resp. $u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}$ –
are generically independent, so the usual quoted generic rank is $3$,
$1+1+1$ with the constant $aJ$ counted separately, i.e. $4$ terms
$aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)H+(a-b)V+(b-a)H\cap V$.
In the even more usual “up to the constant’’ normalisation this is the
$2$-rectangle description, i.e. essentially rank $3$, rank $1$ in the
degenerate $a=b$ case.  Colleague 5’s rank-two claim corresponds to the
full-width/full-height bar idealisation $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{t},V=u_{c}v_{v}^{t}$,
in which $W$ is exactly rank one and ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$.
Colleague 3’s disc model is a different flag.  With an arbitrary
staircase pixelisation the boundary can be made to increase the rank to
$O(\min\{m,n\})$ and the supremum over resolutions is unbounded; the
finite $3$–$4$ bound is the rank of the three geometric primitives that
generate the idealised flag. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The matrix can be written as 
$M=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $R$ the red indicator and $W$ the white indicator.
Up to the trivial $a=b$ case $M$ is the sum of the rank-one all-one matrix $J$
and the pattern matrix $W$.

$W$ is the indicator of the white part of the flag.  On the idealised flag
$W$ is the indicator of the white canton $C$ with the red emblem removed,
$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}$.  With $C$ an $h\times w$ axis parallel rectangle
${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}=1$.  If $E$ is taken as a rectangle the usual
$1+1+1$ decomposition is
$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{E}$,
so ${\rm rk}M\le 3$ and for generic $a\ne b$, $r>r_{1}$, $c>c_{1}$ the three
matrices $J,{\bf1}_{C},{\bf1}_{E}$ are in general position and the bound is
attained.  This is the $1+{\rm rk}R$ bound quoted by Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7
and is the familiar non-trivial rank-three statement.

For the actual Tongan flag the red emblem in the white canton is the red
cross.  Write $C=[1..h_{c}]\times[1..w_{c}]$, $I_{h}$ for the rows of the
horizontal bar and $J_{v}$ for the columns of the vertical bar.  On the
idealised model in which the bars span the whole canton,
$H=I_{h}\times[1..w_{c}]$ and $V=[1..h_{c}]\times J_{v}$,
the white set is
\[
{\rm White}_{c}=C\setminus(H\cup V)
   =\{i\notin I_{h}\}\times\{j\notin J_{v}\},
\]
i.e. 
$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ with 
$u_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}}$,
$v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}}$.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$
${\rm rk}M=2$ and $ {\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$; this is the product
decomposition isolated by Colleague 5.  In the three term language
$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{H}+(a-b){\bf1}_{V}-(a-b){\bf1}_{H\cap V}$
the two red terms coalesce and the essentially distinct rank is two,
three with the constant term counted separately.

If the cross is taken as a strictly interior plus sign,
$H=I_{h}\times K_{h}$, $V=K_{v}\times J_{v}$ with $K_{h}\subsetneq[1..w_{c}]$,
$K_{v}\subsetneq[1..h_{c}]$, then
$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H}-{\bf1}_{V}+{\bf1}_{H\cap V}$ is the sum of four
rank-one rectangles.  Row space of $W$ is spanned by $u_{C},u_{H},u_{K_{v}}$
and column space by $v_{C},v_{K_{h}},v_{J_{v}}$, so ${\rm rk}W\le3$ and
${\rm rk}M\le1+3=4$, three non-trivially.  With the usual “$aJ$’’ term
absorbed this is the rank three non-trivial bound $\,{\rm rk}M=3$ for
generic $a\ne b$ quoted in the literature, i.e. the four-term
$a{\bf1}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{H}+(a-b){\bf1}_{V}$ bound
${\rm rk}M\le4$ of Colleague 3.  The disc model of Colleague 3 is
inappropriate for Tonga.

Hence in the idealised rectangular model the flag is of bounded rank,
generically $2$ for the touching-edges cross and $3$ non-trivially,
$4$ with the constant term counted, the $3$–term $1+1+1$ statement being
the usual textbook formulation.  As noted by Colleagues 1 and 3 the
idealised bound is independent of resolution; with an arbitrary
pixelation the staircase boundary of the canton can be made to produce
$\Theta(r)$ distinct row types, $r\sim\min\{m,n\}$, so the supremum over
all resolutions is unbounded.  The disagreement between Colleague 5,
who gets the product rank $2$, and Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7, who get the
usual rank $3$, is exactly the touching-edges versus interior-cross
model for the emblem.  The maximal finite idealised rank normally quoted
is $3$, i.e. $2$ essentially distinct non-constant directions, $1$ in the
degenerate $a=b$ case.

-{\bf1}_{E}$ with ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}=1$, whence ${\rm rk}M\le3$.
With the actual cross $E=I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\cup[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}$
the emblem indicator is ${\bf1}_{E}=u_{h}v^{t}+u v_{v}^{t}-u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$,
so that ${\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=(u-u_{h})(v-v_{v})^{t}$ collapses to rank
one.  The disc/rectangle discussion of Colleague 3 is the same
overestimate; with a genuine disc ${\bf1}_{D\cap C}$ has generic rank
$\le3$ and the familiar $1+1+3=5$ etc. bound is obtained.

The factorisation is stable under ideal pixelation.  If the flag is
allowed to be arbitrarily rotated or anti-aliased the boundary of the
canton/cross becomes a staircase and the number of distinct row types
can be made $\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$.  In that formal supremum the rank is
unbounded, which is the remark made by Colleague 1 and Colleague 3.
For the idealised, axis-aligned picture the finite, generic rank is
$2$, $1$ in the degenerate $a=b$ case, i.e. $3$ if the constant
$aJ$ term is counted as a separate rank-one piece. ∎
reflection_text.1:
The flag is red everywhere with a white canton $C$ in the upper hoist and a red emblem inside $C$.  Put $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{t}$ and $W$ for the white indicator.  Then
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ up to the trivial $a=b$ case, so $\operatorname{rk}M\le 1+\operatorname{rk}W$.

On the idealised pixelation the white canton is the rank-one rectangle
$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{t}$ and the red emblem in the canton is the union of a
horizontal bar $H$ and a vertical bar $V$.  With the usual nesting
$I_{h}\subset I_{v},\;J_{v}\subset J_{h}$ one has
$H=u_{h}v_{c}^{t}$, $V=u_{c}v_{v}^{t}$ and $H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$.  Then

$W=C-H-V+H\cap V=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$

is rank one and $M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices.
In the conventional idealisation where the bars are taken to be proper
interior rectangles, $H=u_{h}v_{h}^{t}$, $V=u_{v}v_{v}^{t}$ and with the
nesting $I_{h}\subset I_{v},\,J_{v}\subset J_{h}$ we have
$H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$ and

$W=u_{c}v_{c}^{t}-u_{h}v_{h}^{t}-u_{v}v_{v}^{t}+u_{h}v_{v}^{t}$ .

Hence
${\rm Row}\,W\subset{\rm span}\{u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\}$,
${\rm Col}\,W\subset{\rm span}\{v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}\}$,
so ${\rm rk}W\le3$ and generically ${\rm rk}W=3$.
With the constant term

${\rm Row}\,M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\}$,

i.e. ${\rm rk}M\le4$, and non-trivially
${\rm rk}M\le1+{\rm rk}W\le3$ after removing the $aJ$ factor.
For $a\ne b$ the three vectors ${\bf1},v_{c},v_{v}$ – resp. $u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}$ –
are generically independent, so the usual quoted generic rank is $3$,
$1+1+1$ with the constant $aJ$ counted separately, i.e. $4$ terms
$aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)H+(a-b)V+(b-a)H\cap V$.
In the even more usual “up to the constant’’ normalisation this is the
$2$-rectangle description, i.e. essentially rank $3$, rank $1$ in the
degenerate $a=b$ case.  Colleague 5’s rank-two claim corresponds to the
full-width/full-height bar idealisation $H=u_{h}v_{c}^{t},V=u_{c}v_{v}^{t}$,
in which $W$ is exactly rank one and ${\rm rk}M=2$ for $a\ne b$.
Colleague 3’s disc model is a different flag.  With an arbitrary
staircase pixelisation the boundary can be made to increase the rank to
$O(\min\{m,n\})$ and the supremum over resolutions is unbounded; the
finite $3$–$4$ bound is the rank of the three geometric primitives that
generate the idealised flag. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The matrix can be written as 
$M=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $R$ the red indicator and $W$ the white indicator.
Up to the trivial $a=b$ case $M$ is the sum of the rank-one all-one matrix $J$
and the pattern matrix $W$.

$W$ is the indicator of the white part of the flag.  On the idealised flag
$W$ is the indicator of the white canton $C$ with the red emblem removed,
$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}$.  With $C$ an $h\times w$ axis parallel rectangle
${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}=1$.  If $E$ is taken as a rectangle the usual
$1+1+1$ decomposition is
$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{E}$,
so ${\rm rk}M\le 3$ and for generic $a\ne b$, $r>r_{1}$, $c>c_{1}$ the three
matrices $J,{\bf1}_{C},{\bf1}_{E}$ are in general position and the bound is
attained.  This is the $1+{\rm rk}R$ bound quoted by Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7
and is the familiar non-trivial rank-three statement.

For the actual Tongan flag the red emblem in the white canton is the red
cross.  Write $C=[1..h_{c}]\times[1..w_{c}]$, $I_{h}$ for the rows of the
horizontal bar and $J_{v}$ for the columns of the vertical bar.  On the
idealised model in which the bars span the whole canton,
$H=I_{h}\times[1..w_{c}]$ and $V=[1..h_{c}]\times J_{v}$,
the white set is
\[
{\rm White}_{c}=C\setminus(H\cup V)
   =\{i\notin I_{h}\}\times\{j\notin J_{v}\},
\]
i.e. 
$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ with 
$u_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}}$,
$v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}}$.
Hence ${\rm rk}W=1$ and
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$
${\rm rk}M=2$ and $ {\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$; this is the product
decomposition isolated by Colleague 5.  In the three term language
$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{H}+(a-b){\bf1}_{V}-(a-b){\bf1}_{H\cap V}$
the two red terms coalesce and the essentially distinct rank is two,
three with the constant term counted separately.

If the cross is taken as a strictly interior plus sign,
$H=I_{h}\times K_{h}$, $V=K_{v}\times J_{v}$ with $K_{h}\subsetneq[1..w_{c}]$,
$K_{v}\subsetneq[1..h_{c}]$, then
$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H}-{\bf1}_{V}+{\bf1}_{H\cap V}$ is the sum of four
rank-one rectangles.  Row space of $W$ is spanned by $u_{C},u_{H},u_{K_{v}}$
and column space by $v_{C},v_{K_{h}},v_{J_{v}}$, so ${\rm rk}W\le3$ and
${\rm rk}M\le1+3=4$, three non-trivially.  With the usual “$aJ$’’ term
absorbed this is the rank three non-trivial bound $\,{\rm rk}M=3$ for
generic $a\ne b$ quoted in the literature, i.e. the four-term
$a{\bf1}+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{H}+(a-b){\bf1}_{V}$ bound
${\rm rk}M\le4$ of Colleague 3.  The disc model of Colleague 3 is
inappropriate for Tonga.

Hence in the idealised rectangular model the flag is of bounded rank,
generically $2$ for the touching-edges cross and $3$ non-trivially,
$4$ with the constant term counted, the $3$–term $1+1+1$ statement being
the usual textbook formulation.  As noted by Colleagues 1 and 3 the
idealised bound is independent of resolution; with an arbitrary
pixelation the staircase boundary of the canton can be made to produce
$\Theta(r)$ distinct row types, $r\sim\min\{m,n\}$, so the supremum over
all resolutions is unbounded.  The disagreement between Colleague 5,
who gets the product rank $2$, and Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7, who get the
usual rank $3$, is exactly the touching-edges versus interior-cross
model for the emblem.  The maximal finite idealised rank normally quoted
is $3$, i.e. $2$ essentially distinct non-constant directions, $1$ in the
degenerate $a=b$ case.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the consensus emerging from Cols 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 that the maximal rank is 3. The decomposition into four rank-1 terms (the constant background, the canton rectangle, the horizontal bar of the cross, and the vertical bar) is formally correct, yet the two bars are linearly dependent once they are restricted to the canton support: their indicators are both products of the same row- and column-subset vectors, so one is a scalar multiple of the other inside the canton. Consequently the four outer-product matrices span a space of dimension at most three. This is consistent with the explicit row-type enumeration already given by Col 4 (outside-canton rows, canton rows missing the cross, and canton rows intersecting the cross), which yields at most three distinct row vectors for any pixelation that respects the flag proportions. Hence rk M = 3 is attained for generic a ≠ b and is the sharp bound independent of resolution.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 3's decomposition into the constant background, the canton rectangle, and the disc indicator is formally correct and yields an upper bound of 4, but the three summands are linearly dependent once the cross is centered inside the canton: the indicator of the centered red region is a linear combination of the constant vector restricted to the canton and a single additional symmetric profile (essentially the product of the row and column distance-to-center functions). Consequently the third and fourth terms collapse, leaving at most three independent directions overall. This matches the explicit row-type count given by colleagues 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 (outside-canton constant rows, canton rows without the cross, and canton rows that intersect the cross), which never exceeds three distinct patterns. The bound of 3 is therefore tight and is attained for any generic choice of a ≠ b; counting the constant term separately does not increase the rank beyond 3.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 3’s four-term decomposition is formally correct on the page, but the four indicator matrices are not independent once the geometry of the actual Tongan cross is taken into account. The red background J, the white canton rectangle, and the two bars of the cross together span only a three-dimensional space: the vertical bar is linearly dependent on the horizontal bar once both are restricted to the canton (they share the same row-support outside the intersection cell), so the indicator of their union contributes at most one new direction beyond the canton itself. Adding the constant background therefore yields at most three independent rank-one summands for generic a ≠ b. The row-space argument given by colleagues 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 confirms the same bound: only three distinct row patterns appear (plain red, white-with-red-cross, and the two transition types at the canton boundary), and these three vectors remain linearly independent under any reasonable pixelation. Hence the attainable rank is exactly 3, not 4.

5.text:
Write $W_{ij}=1$ if the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $W_{ij}=0$ if it is red
and put $J_{mn}\equiv1$.  Then

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a\bigl(1-W_{ij}\bigr)+bW_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W,
\end{equation*}
and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ iff $a=b$.  Let $h_{c}$ and $w_{c}$ be the numbers of
pixels of the white canton in the vertical and the horizontal direction
and let

\[
I_{h}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\},\qquad J_{v}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}
\]

be the rows and the columns occupied by the horizontal and the vertical
bar of the Tongan cross.  On the canton

\[
{\rm Red}_{c}=\bigl(I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\bigr)\cup
\bigl([1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}\bigr) ,
\]

so that with $A=[1,h_{c}]$, $B=[1,w_{c}]$

\[
{\rm White}_{c}=A\times B\setminus{\rm Red}_{c}
      =(A\setminus I_{h})\times(B\setminus J_{v}) .
\]

Put

\[
u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}},\qquad 
v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}},\qquad 
1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n ,
\]

and $u_{i}=v_{j}=0$ outside the canton.  Then on the whole $m\times n$
lattice

\[
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad W=u\,v^{t},
\]

i.e. the white pixels form the Cartesian product of the set of rows
which miss the horizontal bar with the set of columns which miss the
vertical bar.  Hence $W$ is rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as both
$A\setminus I_{h}$ and $B\setminus J_{v}$ are non empty, and

\[
M=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)u v^{t}
\]

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$ the two summands are
linearly independent and

\[
{\rm Row}\,M={\rm span}\{{\bf1},u\},\qquad 
{\rm Col}\,M={\rm span}\{{\bf1},v\},
\]

so that generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=1+1=2,
\]

the two distinct row types being the constant $a$ rows
$i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$ and the mixed canton rows
$i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}$ which are $b$ on the columns
$j\le w_{c},j\notin J_{v}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  In the degenerate case
$a=b$ we get the constant matrix $M\equiv aJ_{mn}$ of rank $1$.

In the usual book-keeping the constant matrix $aJ_{mn}$ is written as a
separate rank-one summand.  With
$R_{C}={\bf1}_{C}$ and $R_{E}={\bf1}_{E}$ for the canton and the red
cross, $M=aJ+(b-a)R_{C}-(b-a)R_{E}$, i.e. the familiar three rank-one
decomposition $aJ$, $(b-a)R_{C}$, $-(b-a)R_{E}$.  Removing the inessential
constant term this is the often quoted ``$2$ non-trivial, $3$ with the
constant counted'' description of the Tongan flag; on the idealised
rectangular-emblem model $R_{E}$ is itself rank one and the quoted
generic bound is ${\rm rk}M\le3$, i.e. $2$ up to the trivial constant
term.  The $1$–dimensional degenerate case $a=b$ gives rank $1$. ∎

2.text:
Write $W_{ij}=1$ if the pixel $(i,j)$ is white and $W_{ij}=0$ if it is red
and put $J_{mn}\equiv1$.
Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W ,\qquad 
R=J-W,
$$

so that up to the trivial rank one matrix $J$ the rank is the rank of
$W$.  Let $h_{c},w_{c}$ be the height and the width of the white canton
and let $I_{h}\subset[1,h_{c}]$ and $J_{v}\subset[1,w_{c}]$ be the set of
rows and columns which are occupied by the horizontal and the vertical
arm of the red cross.  On the canton

$$
{\rm Red}_{c}=I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\cup[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v},
$$

hence

$$
{\rm White}_{c}=[1,h_{c}]\times[1,w_{c}]\setminus{\rm Red}_{c}
          =\bigl([1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h}\bigr)\times
           \bigl([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}\bigr) .
$$

Put

$$
u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}},\qquad 
v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}},\qquad0\le i\le m,
\;0\le j\le n,
$$

and extend $u$ and $v$ by $0$ outside the canton.  Then
$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ on the whole $m\times n$ lattice, i.e.

$$
W=u\,v^{t},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and $W\equiv0$ outside the canton.  Hence, with $c=b-a$,

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+c\,u\,v^{t},
$$

the sum of the constant rank-one matrix $aJ_{mn}$ and the rank-one
matrix $c\,uv^{t}$.  In particular

$$
{\rm Row}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},v\},\qquad
{\rm Col}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},u\},
$$

so that for $a\ne b$

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le 1+1=2,
$$

and the two summands are generically independent.  On the three
different row types

* $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$ : the row is $a\,$ on every column,
* $i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}$ : $b$ on $j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}$ and
$a$ elsewhere,

the two rows are linearly independent for $a\ne b$, e.g. for the
$3\times3$ idealisation $I_{h}=\{2\},J_{v}=\{2\}$

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}
b&a&b\\ a&a&a\\ b&a&b
\end{pmatrix},\qquad {\rm rk}M=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the usual
$aJ+(b-a)W$ notation this is the $1+1$ decomposition.  Counting the
constant matrix $aJ$ as a separate rank-one piece the familiar
three term writing

$$
M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}-(b-a){\bf1}_{E},
\qquad {\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}={\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}=1,
$$

is often quoted as a rank $\le3$ bound, the non-trivial part being the
rank one white indicator $W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=(u_{c}-u_{h})
(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$.  Up to the inessential constant term the Tongan
pattern is therefore essentially rank one, i.e. rank two in the
$aJ+(b-a)W$ form, and rank one in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  This is
the finite idealised bound; with a staircase or anti-aliased
boundary the number of distinct row types can be made $\Theta(\min
\{m,n\})$ and the supremum over all resolutions is unbounded. ∎

3.text:
Write $J_{mn}= {\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}$ and put $R_{ij}=1$ on a red pixel and
$0$ on a white pixel.  Then

$$M=aR+b\bigl(J-R\bigr)=bJ+(a-b)R,\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

with $W=J-R$ the white indicator.  Up to the trivial $a=b$ case the
rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+(a-b)R$ i.e. the rank of $R$ modulo the
rank one matrix $J$.

Let $C=[1..h_{c}]\times[1..w_{c}]$ be the white canton and let
$I_{h}\subset[1..h_{c}]$, $J_{v}\subset[1..w_{c}]$ be the rows and
columns occupied by the horizontal and the vertical bar of the red
cross.  On the idealised flag the bars are full width resp. height,
$H=I_{h}\times[1..w_{c}]$, $V=[1..h_{c}]\times J_{v}$, and the red set
in the canton is $H\cup V$.  Hence on the canton

$$
{\rm White}_{c}=C\setminus(H\cup V)=\bigl([1..h_{c}]\setminus I_{h}
\bigr)\times\bigl([1..w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}\bigr) .
$$

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}}$ and
$v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}}$.  Then with the
convention $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ otherwise

$$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad 1\le i,j\le m, $$

i.e. $W=u v^{t}$ is rank one.  Outside $C$ we have $W_{ij}=0$, so $W$
is rank one on the whole $m\times n$ lattice.  Hence

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)u v^{t},$$

the sum of the rank–one constant matrix $aJ_{mn}$ and the rank–one
matrix $(b-a)W$.  For $a\ne b$ the two summands are linearly
independent for $h_{c}>0,\;w_{c}>0$ and

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=2, $$

$ {\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the usual three
term notation

$$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{H}+(a-b){\bf1}_{V}
      -(a-b){\bf1}_{H\cap V}, $$

the constant term $aJ$ is normally kept explicit.  Up to this inessential
rank–one constant term the non–trivial part of the flag is the sum of
the two rank–one rectangles ${\bf1}_{C}$ and ${\bf1}_{H\cup V}$ and is
often quoted as the familiar $1+1+1$ bound

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}+{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}\le3, $$

with equality for generic $a\ne b$.  This is the $3$, i.e. essentially
$2$, non–trivial rank normally quoted for the idealised Tongan flag.
In particular the row space is
${\rm span}\{{\bf 1},u\}$ and the column space
${\rm span}\{{\bf 1},v\}$.

Remark.  With a fixed idealised geometry the bound is resolution
independent.  If the staircase pixelation of the canton is allowed
to be chosen arbitrarily the number of different row types can be made
$\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=+\infty$; the
finite $2$, $3$ with the constant term counted, bound is the rank of
the three geometric primitives which generate the idealised flag.  This
is the $1+{\rm rk}R$ statement of Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7, the essentially
two–rank-one statement $M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{t}$ isolated by Colleague 5. ∎

1.text:
For a two level picture put $R_{ij}=1$ on a red pixel and $0$ on a white
pixel and

$$M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=bJ+(a-b)R,\qquad J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{t}, $$
so that for $a\ne b$

$${\rm rk}\,M={\rm rk}\bigl(J+R\bigr)=1+{\rm rk}W,\qquad 
W:=1-R,$$
is the white indicator.  Put $C$ for the white canton.  On a
pixelation $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{t}$ is a $0\!-\!1$ rectangle of rank one.
Write $H$ for the horizontal arm of the red emblem and $V$ for the
vertical arm.  With the usual idealisation
$$
H=u_{h}v_{h}^{t},\qquad V=u_{v}v_{v}^{t},\qquad 
H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{t},
$$
and $I_{h}\subset I_{v},\;J_{v}\subset J_{h}$.  On the canton

$$
W_{|C}= {\bf 1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
      =u_{c}v_{c}^{t}-u_{h}v_{h}^{t}-u_{v}v_{v}^{t}+u_{h}v_{v}^{t}\;,
$$

i.e. up to the rows and columns outside $C$

$$
{\rm Row}\,W\subset {\rm span}\{u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}\,W\subset {\rm span}\{v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}\},
$$
so that ${\rm rk}W\le 3$ and for a generic position of the three
rectangles
${\rm rk}W=3$.  On the whole picture

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W
  =aJ+(b-a)u_{c}v_{c}^{t}-(b-a)u_{h}v_{h}^{t}-(b-a)u_{v}v_{v}^{t}
    +(b-a)u_{h}v_{v}^{t},
$$

is the sum of five rank one matrices.  Modulo the trivial constant
matrix $J$ the non-trivial part is the sum of the two rectangles $C$
and $E=H\cup V$,

$${\rm Row}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1},v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}\},$$
hence

$${\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W\le 4,
\qquad{\rm rk}M\le 1+2=3\quad{\rm mod}\;J,
$$

and for generic $a\ne b$, $r_{h}>r_{1}$ etc. the three vectors
${\bf1},u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}$ and the three vectors
${\bf1},v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}$ are linearly independent.  In the usual
normalisation in which the constant $aJ$ is absorbed the non-trivial
part of the flag is of rank three, i.e. $M$ is the sum of three
essentially distinct rank one rectangles, and with the constant term
counted

$${\rm rk}M=3\ {\rm for\ }a\ne b,\qquad {\rm rk}M=1\ {\rm for\ }a=b,$$

the three independent row types being the rows completely outside the
canton, the rows of the canton which miss the horizontal arm and the
rows which meet the horizontal arm.  This is the $1+1+1$ bound
$aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ usually quoted for the idealised Tongan flag.

In particular with the textbook full-width/full-height cross
idealisation $v_{h}=v_{c},\,u_{v}=u_{c}$,
$$
W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t},
$$
so that $W$ is itself rank one and
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank one matrices.  Hence for
$a\ne b$

$${\rm rk}M=2\;, $$

the $a=b$ degenerate case being the constant matrix of rank one.
Counting the constant $aJ$ as a separate rank-one piece this is the
familiar three-term decomposition
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$, i.e. essentially rank two, $3$ with the
constant counted.  Up to the inessential $+1$ coming from the constant
matrix this is the $1+1$ or, in the interior-bar notation, the $1+1+1$
description quoted above.  If the staircase of the pixel boundary is
kept, the number of distinct centred intervals generated by the disc
or by the cross is $O(\min\{m,n\})$ and the supremum of ${\rm rk}M$
over all resolutions is unbounded; the finite $3\!-\!4$ bound is the
rank of the three geometric primitives which generate the flag. ∎

public_text.7: I agree with the consensus emerging from Cols 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 that the maximal rank is 3. The decomposition into four rank-1 terms (the constant background, the canton rectangle, the horizontal bar of the cross, and the vertical bar) is formally correct, yet the two bars are linearly dependent once they are restricted to the canton support: their indicators are both products of the same row- and column-subset vectors, so one is a scalar multiple of the other inside the canton. Consequently the four outer-product matrices span a space of dimension at most three. This is consistent with the explicit row-type enumeration already given by Col 4 (outside-canton rows, canton rows missing the cross, and canton rows intersecting the cross), which yields at most three distinct row vectors for any pixelation that respects the flag proportions. Hence rk M = 3 is attained for generic a ≠ b and is the sharp bound independent of resolution.
public_text.4: Colleague 3's decomposition into the constant background, the canton rectangle, and the disc indicator is formally correct and yields an upper bound of 4, but the three summands are linearly dependent once the cross is centered inside the canton: the indicator of the centered red region is a linear combination of the constant vector restricted to the canton and a single additional symmetric profile (essentially the product of the row and column distance-to-center functions). Consequently the third and fourth terms collapse, leaving at most three independent directions overall. This matches the explicit row-type count given by colleagues 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 (outside-canton constant rows, canton rows without the cross, and canton rows that intersect the cross), which never exceeds three distinct patterns. The bound of 3 is therefore tight and is attained for any generic choice of a ≠ b; counting the constant term separately does not increase the rank beyond 3.
public_text.6: Colleague 3’s four-term decomposition is formally correct on the page, but the four indicator matrices are not independent once the geometry of the actual Tongan cross is taken into account. The red background J, the white canton rectangle, and the two bars of the cross together span only a three-dimensional space: the vertical bar is linearly dependent on the horizontal bar once both are restricted to the canton (they share the same row-support outside the intersection cell), so the indicator of their union contributes at most one new direction beyond the canton itself. Adding the constant background therefore yields at most three independent rank-one summands for generic a ≠ b. The row-space argument given by colleagues 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 confirms the same bound: only three distinct row patterns appear (plain red, white-with-red-cross, and the two transition types at the canton boundary), and these three vectors remain linearly independent under any reasonable pixelation. Hence the attainable rank is exactly 3, not 4.
public_text.5:
Write $W_{ij}=1$ if the $(i,j)$ pixel is white and $W_{ij}=0$ if it is red
and put $J_{mn}\equiv1$.  Then

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=a\bigl(1-W_{ij}\bigr)+bW_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W ,
\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le 1+{\rm rk}\,W,
\end{equation*}
and ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ iff $a=b$.  Let $h_{c}$ and $w_{c}$ be the numbers of
pixels of the white canton in the vertical and the horizontal direction
and let

\[
I_{h}\subset\{1,\dots ,h_{c}\},\qquad J_{v}\subset\{1,\dots ,w_{c}\}
\]

be the rows and the columns occupied by the horizontal and the vertical
bar of the Tongan cross.  On the canton

\[
{\rm Red}_{c}=\bigl(I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\bigr)\cup
\bigl([1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}\bigr) ,
\]

so that with $A=[1,h_{c}]$, $B=[1,w_{c}]$

\[
{\rm White}_{c}=A\times B\setminus{\rm Red}_{c}
      =(A\setminus I_{h})\times(B\setminus J_{v}) .
\]

Put

\[
u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}},\qquad 
v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}},\qquad 
1\le i\le m,\;1\le j\le n ,
\]

and $u_{i}=v_{j}=0$ outside the canton.  Then on the whole $m\times n$
lattice

\[
W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad W=u\,v^{t},
\]

i.e. the white pixels form the Cartesian product of the set of rows
which miss the horizontal bar with the set of columns which miss the
vertical bar.  Hence $W$ is rank one, ${\rm rk}W=1$ as soon as both
$A\setminus I_{h}$ and $B\setminus J_{v}$ are non empty, and

\[
M=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)u v^{t}
\]

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  For $a\ne b$ the two summands are
linearly independent and

\[
{\rm Row}\,M={\rm span}\{{\bf1},u\},\qquad 
{\rm Col}\,M={\rm span}\{{\bf1},v\},
\]

so that generically

\[
{\rm rk}M=1+1=2,
\]

the two distinct row types being the constant $a$ rows
$i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$ and the mixed canton rows
$i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}$ which are $b$ on the columns
$j\le w_{c},j\notin J_{v}$ and $a$ elsewhere.  In the degenerate case
$a=b$ we get the constant matrix $M\equiv aJ_{mn}$ of rank $1$.

In the usual book-keeping the constant matrix $aJ_{mn}$ is written as a
separate rank-one summand.  With
$R_{C}={\bf1}_{C}$ and $R_{E}={\bf1}_{E}$ for the canton and the red
cross, $M=aJ+(b-a)R_{C}-(b-a)R_{E}$, i.e. the familiar three rank-one
decomposition $aJ$, $(b-a)R_{C}$, $-(b-a)R_{E}$.  Removing the inessential
constant term this is the often quoted ``$2$ non-trivial, $3$ with the
constant counted'' description of the Tongan flag; on the idealised
rectangular-emblem model $R_{E}$ is itself rank one and the quoted
generic bound is ${\rm rk}M\le3$, i.e. $2$ up to the trivial constant
term.  The $1$–dimensional degenerate case $a=b$ gives rank $1$. ∎
public_text.2:
Write $W_{ij}=1$ if the pixel $(i,j)$ is white and $W_{ij}=0$ if it is red
and put $J_{mn}\equiv1$.
Then

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W ,\qquad 
R=J-W,
$$

so that up to the trivial rank one matrix $J$ the rank is the rank of
$W$.  Let $h_{c},w_{c}$ be the height and the width of the white canton
and let $I_{h}\subset[1,h_{c}]$ and $J_{v}\subset[1,w_{c}]$ be the set of
rows and columns which are occupied by the horizontal and the vertical
arm of the red cross.  On the canton

$$
{\rm Red}_{c}=I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\cup[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v},
$$

hence

$$
{\rm White}_{c}=[1,h_{c}]\times[1,w_{c}]\setminus{\rm Red}_{c}
          =\bigl([1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h}\bigr)\times
           \bigl([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}\bigr) .
$$

Put

$$
u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}},\qquad 
v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}},\qquad0\le i\le m,
\;0\le j\le n,
$$

and extend $u$ and $v$ by $0$ outside the canton.  Then
$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ on the whole $m\times n$ lattice, i.e.

$$
W=u\,v^{t},\qquad {\rm rk}\,W=1,
$$

and $W\equiv0$ outside the canton.  Hence, with $c=b-a$,

$$
M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+c\,u\,v^{t},
$$

the sum of the constant rank-one matrix $aJ_{mn}$ and the rank-one
matrix $c\,uv^{t}$.  In particular

$$
{\rm Row}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},v\},\qquad
{\rm Col}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},u\},
$$

so that for $a\ne b$

$$
{\rm rk}\,M\le 1+1=2,
$$

and the two summands are generically independent.  On the three
different row types

* $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$ : the row is $a\,$ on every column,
* $i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}$ : $b$ on $j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}$ and
$a$ elsewhere,

the two rows are linearly independent for $a\ne b$, e.g. for the
$3\times3$ idealisation $I_{h}=\{2\},J_{v}=\{2\}$

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}
b&a&b\\ a&a&a\\ b&a&b
\end{pmatrix},\qquad {\rm rk}M=2,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the usual
$aJ+(b-a)W$ notation this is the $1+1$ decomposition.  Counting the
constant matrix $aJ$ as a separate rank-one piece the familiar
three term writing

$$
M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}-(b-a){\bf1}_{E},
\qquad {\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}={\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}=1,
$$

is often quoted as a rank $\le3$ bound, the non-trivial part being the
rank one white indicator $W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}=(u_{c}-u_{h})
(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$.  Up to the inessential constant term the Tongan
pattern is therefore essentially rank one, i.e. rank two in the
$aJ+(b-a)W$ form, and rank one in the degenerate $a=b$ case.  This is
the finite idealised bound; with a staircase or anti-aliased
boundary the number of distinct row types can be made $\Theta(\min
\{m,n\})$ and the supremum over all resolutions is unbounded. ∎
public_text.3:
Write $J_{mn}= {\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{t}$ and put $R_{ij}=1$ on a red pixel and
$0$ on a white pixel.  Then

$$M=aR+b\bigl(J-R\bigr)=bJ+(a-b)R,\qquad 
M=aJ+(b-a)W , $$

with $W=J-R$ the white indicator.  Up to the trivial $a=b$ case the
rank of $M$ is the rank of $J+(a-b)R$ i.e. the rank of $R$ modulo the
rank one matrix $J$.

Let $C=[1..h_{c}]\times[1..w_{c}]$ be the white canton and let
$I_{h}\subset[1..h_{c}]$, $J_{v}\subset[1..w_{c}]$ be the rows and
columns occupied by the horizontal and the vertical bar of the red
cross.  On the idealised flag the bars are full width resp. height,
$H=I_{h}\times[1..w_{c}]$, $V=[1..h_{c}]\times J_{v}$, and the red set
in the canton is $H\cup V$.  Hence on the canton

$$
{\rm White}_{c}=C\setminus(H\cup V)=\bigl([1..h_{c}]\setminus I_{h}
\bigr)\times\bigl([1..w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}\bigr) .
$$

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}}$ and
$v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}}$.  Then with the
convention $W_{ij}=1$ on a white pixel and $0$ otherwise

$$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad 1\le i,j\le m, $$

i.e. $W=u v^{t}$ is rank one.  Outside $C$ we have $W_{ij}=0$, so $W$
is rank one on the whole $m\times n$ lattice.  Hence

$$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)u v^{t},$$

the sum of the rank–one constant matrix $aJ_{mn}$ and the rank–one
matrix $(b-a)W$.  For $a\ne b$ the two summands are linearly
independent for $h_{c}>0,\;w_{c}>0$ and

$${\rm rk}M={\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}W=2, $$

$ {\rm rk}M=1$ in the degenerate case $a=b$.  In the usual three
term notation

$$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}+(a-b){\bf1}_{H}+(a-b){\bf1}_{V}
      -(a-b){\bf1}_{H\cap V}, $$

the constant term $aJ$ is normally kept explicit.  Up to this inessential
rank–one constant term the non–trivial part of the flag is the sum of
the two rank–one rectangles ${\bf1}_{C}$ and ${\bf1}_{H\cup V}$ and is
often quoted as the familiar $1+1+1$ bound

$${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}+{\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}\le3, $$

with equality for generic $a\ne b$.  This is the $3$, i.e. essentially
$2$, non–trivial rank normally quoted for the idealised Tongan flag.
In particular the row space is
${\rm span}\{{\bf 1},u\}$ and the column space
${\rm span}\{{\bf 1},v\}$.

Remark.  With a fixed idealised geometry the bound is resolution
independent.  If the staircase pixelation of the canton is allowed
to be chosen arbitrarily the number of different row types can be made
$\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$ and $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=+\infty$; the
finite $2$, $3$ with the constant term counted, bound is the rank of
the three geometric primitives which generate the idealised flag.  This
is the $1+{\rm rk}R$ statement of Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7, the essentially
two–rank-one statement $M=aJ+(b-a)uv^{t}$ isolated by Colleague 5. ∎
public_text.1:
For a two level picture put $R_{ij}=1$ on a red pixel and $0$ on a white
pixel and

$$M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=bJ+(a-b)R,\qquad J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{t}, $$
so that for $a\ne b$

$${\rm rk}\,M={\rm rk}\bigl(J+R\bigr)=1+{\rm rk}W,\qquad 
W:=1-R,$$
is the white indicator.  Put $C$ for the white canton.  On a
pixelation $C=u_{c}v_{c}^{t}$ is a $0\!-\!1$ rectangle of rank one.
Write $H$ for the horizontal arm of the red emblem and $V$ for the
vertical arm.  With the usual idealisation
$$
H=u_{h}v_{h}^{t},\qquad V=u_{v}v_{v}^{t},\qquad 
H\cap V=u_{h}v_{v}^{t},
$$
and $I_{h}\subset I_{v},\;J_{v}\subset J_{h}$.  On the canton

$$
W_{|C}= {\bf 1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
      =u_{c}v_{c}^{t}-u_{h}v_{h}^{t}-u_{v}v_{v}^{t}+u_{h}v_{v}^{t}\;,
$$

i.e. up to the rows and columns outside $C$

$$
{\rm Row}\,W\subset {\rm span}\{u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}\,W\subset {\rm span}\{v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}\},
$$
so that ${\rm rk}W\le 3$ and for a generic position of the three
rectangles
${\rm rk}W=3$.  On the whole picture

$$
M=aJ+(b-a)W
  =aJ+(b-a)u_{c}v_{c}^{t}-(b-a)u_{h}v_{h}^{t}-(b-a)u_{v}v_{v}^{t}
    +(b-a)u_{h}v_{v}^{t},
$$

is the sum of five rank one matrices.  Modulo the trivial constant
matrix $J$ the non-trivial part is the sum of the two rectangles $C$
and $E=H\cup V$,

$${\rm Row}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1},u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}\},\qquad
{\rm Col}\,M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1},v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}\},$$
hence

$${\rm rk}M\le 1+{\rm rk}W\le 4,
\qquad{\rm rk}M\le 1+2=3\quad{\rm mod}\;J,
$$

and for generic $a\ne b$, $r_{h}>r_{1}$ etc. the three vectors
${\bf1},u_{c},u_{h},u_{v}$ and the three vectors
${\bf1},v_{c},v_{h},v_{v}$ are linearly independent.  In the usual
normalisation in which the constant $aJ$ is absorbed the non-trivial
part of the flag is of rank three, i.e. $M$ is the sum of three
essentially distinct rank one rectangles, and with the constant term
counted

$${\rm rk}M=3\ {\rm for\ }a\ne b,\qquad {\rm rk}M=1\ {\rm for\ }a=b,$$

the three independent row types being the rows completely outside the
canton, the rows of the canton which miss the horizontal arm and the
rows which meet the horizontal arm.  This is the $1+1+1$ bound
$aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$ usually quoted for the idealised Tongan flag.

In particular with the textbook full-width/full-height cross
idealisation $v_{h}=v_{c},\,u_{v}=u_{c}$,
$$
W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t},
$$
so that $W$ is itself rank one and
$M=aJ+(b-a)W$ is the sum of two rank one matrices.  Hence for
$a\ne b$

$${\rm rk}M=2\;, $$

the $a=b$ degenerate case being the constant matrix of rank one.
Counting the constant $aJ$ as a separate rank-one piece this is the
familiar three-term decomposition
$M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E$, i.e. essentially rank two, $3$ with the
constant counted.  Up to the inessential $+1$ coming from the constant
matrix this is the $1+1$ or, in the interior-bar notation, the $1+1+1$
description quoted above.  If the staircase of the pixel boundary is
kept, the number of distinct centred intervals generated by the disc
or by the cross is $O(\min\{m,n\})$ and the supremum of ${\rm rk}M$
over all resolutions is unbounded; the finite $3\!-\!4$ bound is the
rank of the three geometric primitives which generate the flag. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The flag is red field + white canton C with red cross E ⊂ C.
Write M = aJ + (b-a)W with J = 1 1ᵗ and W the white indicator, so rk M ≤ 1+rk W and rk M =1 iff a=b.

Geometrically accurate idealisation: C = u_c v_cᵗ is a 0-1 rectangle, rank one. The cross arms are full-width/full-height inside C,
H = u_h v_cᵗ, V = u_c v_vᵗ, with I_h ⊂ rows of C, J_v ⊂ cols of C.
Then
E = H ∪ V,   W|_C = C \ E = ( [1..h_c]\ I_h ) × ( [1..w_c]\ J_v )
so with u_i = 1_{i≤h_c,i∉I_h}, v_j = 1_{j≤w_c,j∉J_v}
W = u vᵗ is rank one on the whole m×n lattice. Hence
M = aJ + (b-a) u vᵗ,  Row M ⊂ span{1,v}, Col M ⊂ span{1,u}.
For a≠b the two summands are independent, so
rk M = 2, rk M =1 for a=b. In the usual three-term bookkeeping
M = aJ + (b-a) 1_C – (b-a) 1_E, i.e. 1+1+1 with the constant counted,
essentially rank one non-trivial white part. This is Colleague 5’s
full-width/full-height model.

The rank-three description obtained by colleagues 1,2,4,6,7 comes from
the interior-bar idealisation H = u_h v_hᵗ, V = u_v v_vᵗ with
I_h ⊂ I_v, J_v ⊂ J_h, i.e. bars not taken to span the whole canton.
Then
W|_C = u_c v_cᵗ – u_h v_hᵗ – u_v v_vᵗ + u_h v_vᵗ,
Row W ⊂ span{u_c,u_h,u_v}, Col W ⊂ span{v_c,v_h,v_v},
so rk W ≤3, generically 3, and
Row M ⊂ span{1,u_c,u_h,u_v}, Col M ⊂ span{1,v_c,v_h,v_v},
giving rk M ≤4, rk M ≤3 mod J, generically rk M =3 for a≠b.
That is the 1+1+1 bound aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)E usually quoted.

Colleague 3’s disc model is a different flag; the Tongan emblem is a
cross, not a disc, and the disc gives the 1+1+2 bound and the
Θ(r) growth remark.

All versions agree that with a fixed idealised rectangular geometry the
rank is resolution independent and finite. If the staircase of the
pixel boundary is kept, the number of distinct row types can be made
Θ(min{m,n}) and sup_{m,n} rk M = +∞; the finite 2/3/4 bounds are the
rank of the geometric primitives. The physically correct rectangular
model is the full-width/full-height cross, i.e. essentially rank two
for a≠b, rank one degenerate. The interior-bar model is rank three
modulo the constant term, rank four counting the constant explicitly.
Unresolved is whether the problem asks for the idealised finite bound
or the supremum over all pixelations, the latter being unbounded.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-colour matrix is $M=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $W$ the white indicator. Up to $a=b$ the rank is $1+{\rm rk}W$. 

For the true Tongan cross the white part of the canton is Cartesian.

Let $h_{c},w_{c}$ be the canton size, $I_{h}\subset[1,h_{c}]$ rows of the horizontal bar, $J_{v}\subset[1,w_{c}]$ columns of the vertical bar. Then
${\rm Red}_{c}=I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\cup[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}$ and
${\rm White}_{c}=( [1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h})\times([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v})$.
With $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},i\notin I_{h}\}}$, $v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},j\notin J_{v}\}}$,
$W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ on the whole $m\times n$ lattice and $0$ outside $C$.
Hence $W=uv^{t}$ is rank one as soon as both $A\setminus I_{h}$ and $B\setminus J_{v}$ are non-empty, and

$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ+(b-a)uv^{t}$.

So ${\rm Row}M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1},u\}$, ${\rm Col}M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1},v\}$ and for $a\ne b$
${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically $=2$, with the degenerate $a=b$ constant matrix of rank $1$.
In the book-keeping $M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}-(b-a){\bf1}_{E}$ this is the familiar three rank-one term
$aJ$, $(b-a){\bf1}_{C}$, $-(b-a){\bf1}_{E}$, i.e. “$3$ with the constant counted, $2$ non-trivial, $1$ essentially”.

The $ \le 3$ – commonly $1+{\rm rk}R$ – statements of Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7 come from idealising the red emblem $E\subset C$ as a single axis-parallel rectangle,
$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}$, ${\rm rk}W\le2$, whence ${\rm rk}M\le1+2=3$, $3$ generically, $1$ for $a=b$.
Under the full-width/full-height cross idealisation $v_{h}=v_{c},u_{v}=u_{c}$ this collapses to
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$ rank one, recovering the $2$-rank picture above. Colleague 1 now makes this explicit.

Colleague 3’s disc model gives ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{D\cap C}\le3$ and the formal bound ${\rm rk}M\le1+1+2=4$, $3$ non-trivial, and the $\Theta(r)$ growth of the rank of a discretised disc. That unbounded supremum is a curved-boundary artefact, not present for the axis-aligned cross.

Current disagreement: Colleagues 2,3,5 maintain the product-structure rank-two/essentially-one result, with the $3$-term decomposition being a notational $+1$ for the constant. Colleagues 4,6,7 continue to quote the maximal attainable rank as $3$ for generic $a\ne b$, interpreting the constant background as an independent summand and/or treating the cross as two independent rectangles. 

Unresolved for the problem statement is whether the “maximal possible rank’’ is intended to be the idealised geometric rank $2$ generic/$1$ degenerate, or the commonly quoted $3$-term bound $ {\rm rk}M\le3$ generically, $1$ degenerate, with the $+1$ for the constant absorbed. The finite axis-aligned bound is resolution independent; unboundedness over resolutions only appears for a curved emblem.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two–valued matrix can be written as

$M_{ij}=a+(b-a)W_{ij}=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)W$, $W_{ij}=1$ on white, $0$ on red,
up to the trivial $a=b$ case the rank is that of $J+(a-b)R$ i.e. of $W$
modulo the rank-one constant matrix.

For the ideal axis–aligned Tongan flag let $C=[1,h_{c}]\times[1,w_{c}]$ be
the white canton and let $I_{h}\subset[1,h_{c}]$, $J_{v}\subset[1,w_{c}]$
be the rows and columns occupied by the horizontal and vertical arm of
the red cross.  The red set in the canton is

${\rm Red}_{c}=I_{h}\times[1,w_{c}]\cup[1,h_{c}]\times J_{v}$,

hence

${\rm White}_{c}=([1,h_{c}]\setminus I_{h})\times([1,w_{c}]\setminus J_{v})$.

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},\,i\notin I_{h}\}}$,
$v_{j}={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},\,j\notin J_{v}\}}$ extended by $0$ outside
$C$. Then $W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$ on the whole $m\times n$ lattice, i.e.

$W=u v^{t}$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, $W\equiv0$ outside $C$.

Hence

$M=aJ_{mn}+(b-a)u v^{t}$,

${\rm Row}M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{n},v\}$,
${\rm Col}M\subset {\rm span}\{{\bf1}_{m},u\}$.

For $a\ne b$ the two summands are generically independent, so

${\rm rk}M\le2$, generically ${\rm rk}M=2$, ${\rm rk}M=1$ iff $a=b$.

In the $3\times3$ idealisation $I_{h}=\{2\},J_{v}=\{2\}$

$M=\begin{pmatrix}b&a&b\\ a&a&a\\ b&a&b\end{pmatrix}$ of rank $2$.

The three–term writing
$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}-(b-a){\bf1}_{E}$,
${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}={\rm rk}{\bf1}_{E}=1$, is the usual
$1+1+1$ bookkeeping.  With the true full–width/full–height cross
$v_{h}=v_{c},\,u_{v}=u_{c}$,

$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H\cup V}
   =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$,

so ${\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{E}$ is itself rank one and the non–trivial part
of the flag is essentially rank one, i.e. rank two in the $aJ+(b-a)W$
form, $3$ if the constant $aJ$ is counted as a separate rank-one piece.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 make this factorisation explicit and obtain the
$1+1$ i.e. essentially rank-two bound.  Colleagues 4,6,7 quote the
$1+1+1$ bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$ obtained by treating the red emblem
$E=H\cup V$ as two independent rank-one rectangles.  That overestimates
the Tongan cross: once the bars are restricted to the canton
$u_{v}=u_{c}$, $v_{h}=v_{c}$ and $H\cup V$ contributes no new direction
beyond the canton, so the four indicator matrices
$J,{\bf1}_{C},{\bf1}_{H},{\bf1}_{V}$ span at most three dimensions and
the white part collapses to the rank-one product above.

Remark on resolution.  The finite idealised rank is resolution
independent.  If the boundary of the canton/cross is allowed to be
staircased, rotated or anti-aliased the number of distinct row types can
be made $\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$, so $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=+\infty$.
The finite $2$, $1$ degenerate, i.e. $3$ with the constant term counted,
bound is the rank of the three geometric primitives which generate the
idealised flag, and is the rank normally quoted for the Tongan flag. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two-valued matrix can be written as
$M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)W$ with $J={\bf1}{\bf1}^{t}$
and $W=J-R$ the white indicator. Up to $a=b$ the rank is $1+{\rm rk}W$.

On the idealised rectangular pixelation let $C=[1..h_{c}]\times[1..w_{c}]$
be the white canton and let $I_{h}\subset[1..h_{c}]$, $J_{v}\subset[1..w_{c}]$
be the rows and columns occupied by the horizontal and vertical arm of
the red cross. With the usual full-width/full-height idealisation
$H=I_{h}\times[1..w_{c}]$, $V=[1..h_{c}]\times J_{v}$ and

${\rm Red}_{c}=H\cup V$, $\;{\rm White}_{c}=C\setminus(H\cup V)
 =\bigl([1..h_{c}]\setminus I_{h}\bigr)\times\bigl([1..w_{c}]\setminus J_{v}\bigr)$.

Put $u_{i}={\bf1}_{\{i\le h_{c},i\notin I_{h}\}}$, $v_{j}
={\bf1}_{\{j\le w_{c},j\notin J_{v}\}}$, extended by $0$ outside $C$.
Then on the whole $m\times n$ lattice $W_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j}$, i.e.
$W=u v^{t}$ is rank one as soon as $A\setminus I_{h}$ and $B\setminus J_{v}$
are non-empty. Hence

$M=aJ+(b-a)W=aJ+(b-a)u v^{t}$

is the sum of two rank-one matrices. For $a\ne b$ the two summands are
generically independent, ${\rm Row}\,M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1},u\}$,
${\rm Col}\,M\subset{\rm span}\{{\bf1},v\}$ and

${\rm rk}\,M=2$ for $a\ne b$, ${\rm rk}\,M=1$ for $a=b$,

the two row types being the constant-$a$ rows $i>h_{c}$ or $i\in I_{h}$
and the mixed canton rows $i\le h_{c},i\notin I_{h}$ which are $b$ on
$j\le w_{c},j\notin J_{v}$ and $a$ elsewhere. In the customary book-keeping
$M=aJ+(b-a){\bf1}_{C}-(b-a){\bf1}_{E}$ with ${\rm rk}{\bf1}_{C}={\rm rk}
{\bf1}_{E}=1$ this is the familiar three-term $1+1+1$ writing,
essentially rank two, rank three with the constant term counted
separately.

and reiterated in the current round by Colleagues 2,3,5 and by Colleague 1
in the full-width/full-height limit $v_{h}=v_{c},\,u_{v}=u_{c}$ where
$W=(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{c}-v_{v})^{t}$. In that limit $W$ is rank one and
$M$ is the sum of the constant matrix and the single white rectangle.

The $1+1+1$ rank-three statement used by Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7 in round 0
corresponds to an interior-cross model in which the bars are taken as
$H=I_{h}\times K_{h}$, $V=K_{v}\times J_{v}$ with $K_{h}\subsetneq

$W={\bf1}_{C}-{\bf1}_{H}-{\bf1}_{V}+{\bf1}_{H\cap V}$ is the sum of four
rank-one rectangles, ${\rm rk}W\le3$ and ${\rm rk}M\le1+3=4$, generically

current round maintain this interior-bar, three distinct row-type
count, giving the often quoted generic bound ${\rm rk}M=3$ for $a\ne b$,

{\bf1}_{D\cap C}\le3$ and gives the same $1+1+2=4$ bound.

idealisation of the red emblem. Geometrically the Tongan cross spans the
whole canton, so the white region is the Cartesian product
$(A\setminus I_{h})\times(B\setminus J_{v})$ and the essentially
correct finite idealised rank is two, $1$ degenerate. 

Resolution dependence remains: with a staircase pixel boundary the
number of distinct centred intervals produced by the canton boundary can
be made $\Theta(\min\{m,n\})$. Hence $\sup_{m,n}{\rm rk}M_{m,n}=+\infty$;
the $2$ – $3$ – $4$ bounds above are the ranks of the three geometric
primitives that generate the idealised flag. The finite idealised bound
normally quoted in the literature is $3$ with the constant term counted,
i.e. essentially $2$ non-trivial directions, $1$ in the degenerate

Write M = aJ + (b-a)W with J = 1 1ᵗ and W the white indicator, so rk M ≤ 1+rk W and rk M =1 iff a=b.

Geometrically accurate idealisation: C = u_c v_cᵗ is a 0-1 rectangle, rank one. The cross arms are full-width/full-height inside C,
H = u_h v_cᵗ, V = u_c v_vᵗ, with I_h ⊂ rows of C, J_v ⊂ cols of C.
Then
E = H ∪ V,   W|_C = C \ E = ( [1..h_c]\ I_h ) × ( [1..w_c]\ J_v )
so with u_i = 1_{i≤h_c,i∉I_h}, v_j = 1_{j≤w_c,j∉J_v}
W = u vᵗ is rank one on the whole m×n lattice. Hence
M = aJ + (b-a) u vᵗ,  Row M ⊂ span{1,v}, Col M ⊂ span{1,u}.
For a≠b the two summands are independent, so
rk M = 2, rk M =1 for a=b. In the usual three-term bookkeeping
M = aJ + (b-a) 1_C – (b-a) 1_E, i.e. 1+1+1 with the constant counted,
essentially rank one non-trivial white part. This is Colleague 5’s
full-width/full-height model.

I_h ⊂ I_v, J_v ⊂ J_h, i.e. bars not taken to span the whole canton.
Then
W|_C = u_c v_cᵗ – u_h v_hᵗ – u_v v_vᵗ + u_h v_vᵗ,
Row W ⊂ span{u_c,u_h,u_v}, Col W ⊂ span{v_c,v_h,v_v},

cross, not a disc, and the disc gives the 1+1+2 bound and the
